# tract-core 0.21.4, with one hunk changed

Upstream: <https://github.com/sonos/tract>, MIT / Apache-2.0. The licence files
beside this one are theirs and unmodified.

This is a verbatim copy of the published `tract-core` 0.21.4 with a single
change, in `src/model/typed.rs`. Everything else is upstream. To see exactly
what differs:

```bash
cargo download tract-core==0.21.4    # or unpack it from ~/.cargo/registry
diff -ru <pristine> third_party/tract-core
```

## What it fixes

**The vendored plain DFN3 could not be loaded by any released tract.** That
model is the enhancer rung above losing the enhancer altogether — the one that
keeps a slow phone enhancing rather than giving up on it — so this blocked the
feature outright, and it is why the fork exists.

```
running pass codegen: after graph compaction: duplicate name /convt3/Conv.bias
```

`TypedModel::add_const` deduplicates a constant **by value**: if some node
already holds this exact tensor, reuse it. It then mints the node's name
without asking whether *that* is free. Those are two different questions and
only the first was being asked.

`ModelPatch::apply` grafts a patch's constants into the target under the names
they carried inside the patch, where nothing was competing for them. In the
target they can be taken. In DFN3's `erb_dec` they are:

- `/convt3/Conv` has an all-zero bias, so the const `/convt3/Conv.bias` is
  created for it;
- being a zero tensor, the dedup above **shares that same node** as the padding
  value of a *different* convolution's im2col — `/conv0_out/0/Conv.im2col`;
- `/convt3/Conv` is then rewritten, and its replacement bias arrives, by patch,
  under the name `/convt3/Conv.bias`;
- the shared node is still alive serving the other convolution, so the name is
  still in use. Two nodes, one name.

The fix appends `#1`, `#2`… when the wanted name is taken.

## Why it had to be fixed rather than worked around

**Nothing in tract resolves a node by name at evaluation time**, and
`deep_filter` never calls `node_by_name` — only `symbol_table`. So the graph
computes the same answer either way, and this is cosmetic at runtime.

But `check_compact` rejects it, and `check_compact` is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`.
So the model **loads in release and refuses to load in debug**: the shipped app
was fine, and `cargo test` could not exercise the feature at all. That is not a
difference any caller can act on, and it left the rung untestable.

Neither a version bump nor a workaround was available:

| Route | Why not |
|---|---|
| tract 0.21.5 | byte-identical `add_const`; the bug is still there |
| tract ≥ 0.21.6 | drops `Graph::symbol_table`, which `deep_filter` uses |
| Rename the node in the ONNX | the name is generated by tract, not read from the file |
| `[profile.dev.package.tract-core] debug-assertions = false` | hides the check rather than fixing the graph, and would hide real corruption too |

## Dropping this fork

It should not live here forever. It can go the moment either is true:

- the change is upstreamed and released — **it has not been submitted**, and
  doing so is a public pull request against someone else's project, so it is a
  decision for a person rather than something to be done quietly; or
- `deep_filter` stops needing `Graph::symbol_table`, freeing the pin to move to
  a tract that has fixed this some other way.

To drop it: delete this directory and the `[patch.crates-io]` table at the end
of `core/Cargo.toml`, then run `cd core && cargo test` — in **debug**, because
release cannot see this class of fault.
